correctness.rationale: Nodal sampling determinant is 2sinκ(cosκa−cosκ), so singular samples cannot reproduce nonzero endpoint derivative of g(x)=cosκx−cosκ. Invert unisolvent sample matrix; interior cardinal derivative D_11=κsinκa/(cosκ−cosκa). Positive P_11 and SBP central diagonal force sinκa=0, hence a=0 or ±π/κ exclusively. Endpoint SBP equations uniquely fix q0=sinκ/[κ(1+2cosκ)], P0 middle 2(1+cosκ)q0; off-centre q1=sinκ/[κ(2cosκ−1)], P1 middle 2(1−cosκ)q1. Entrywise cross-identity yields complete SBP. As sinκ<0, central positive only κ<4π/3, off only κ<5π/3. For mass=2, mass residual functions H0,H1 decrease strictly (derivatives 2sinκ(κ∓sinκ)) and have opposite endpoint signs, giving unique κ0≈4.028701 and κ1≈5.066777. Hand-checked positivity, derivatives, 3/2π boundary and alias equality; full parametric proof not inferred from 149 sampled frequencies.
